title: Orsen and the Thorn
premise: Jude Sandoval keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, a trade house that smuggles memories, names, and doors across borders that were never meant to hold. When a child named Orsen arrives at his gate speaking a language older than any kingdom, Jude discovers the child is the last living heir of Vessia, a country erased from maps and memory by a bargain the Guild itself brokered. Pursued by the Thorn, an assassin woven from the forgotten country's grief, Jude must lead Orsen to the one door out of Vessia's lingering echo before the child's inherited memories consume him. In the end, Jude chooses truth over loyalty to the Guild: he opens the door, lets Vessia finally die so its people can be remembered rather than preserved, and pays for it by surrendering his own name to the ledgers.
about_author: Theo Okafor is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing colonial-era trade records in West African port cities, an experience that taught him how much history lives in paperwork. He writes fantasy about bureaucracies of the impossible from a small house in Lisbon.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Doors
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A night of routine inventory at the Guild's gatehouse: bottled lullabies, a stolen shadow, a door that opens onto Tuesday. The chapter establishes Jude's meticulous loyalty to the Guild and his quiet loneliness as keeper. Emotional beat: contentment built on willful blindness.

chapters.title: A Knock in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A child appears at the gate at moonset, speaking a language no ledger records — yet Jude understands it without knowing why. The boy carries a brass key shaped like a thorn. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as the gate itself begins to hum.

chapters.title: What the Guild Bought
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He hides Orsen and searches the restricted ledgers, finding a 200-year-old contract: the Guild purchased the nation of Vessia — its borders, its past, its future — from a dying king. Emotional beat: the first crack in Jude's faith.

chapters.title: Orsen
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Inside the child's mind, inherited memories surface unbidden: a harvest festival, a mother's voice, a city burning without fire. He cannot tell which childhood is his own. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief too large for a small body.

chapters.title: The Auditor Arrives
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Magister Corvane, the Guild's auditor, comes to inspect the gatehouse and senses the anomaly. Jude lies for the first time in nineteen years of service. Emotional beat: terror and the strange exhilaration of betrayal.

chapters.title: Thorn
chapters.summary: The Thorn's POV. An assassin grown from Vessia's discarded grief hunts the heir through the city's forgotten alleys, killing those who once traded in Vessian goods. We see it remembers everything the world chose to forget. Emotional beat: sorrow weaponized.

chapters.title: Nine Names for Rain
chapters.summary: Jude and Orsen flee through the Guild's storage vaults, where Orsen's speech unlocks sealed crates of Vessian relics that answer him like old friends. Jude begins learning the language from the boy. Emotional beat: tenderness blooming under pursuit.

chapters.title: The Contract's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He deciphers the contract's final clause: Vessia was not destroyed but stored, and the Guild must return it if a true heir asks in the old tongue — or forfeit everything. Emotional beat: hope entangled with terrible cost.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Corvane corners Jude privately, revealing he knows about the boy — and offers Jude partnership in hiding Orsen forever, erasing the clause, keeping the Guild's empire intact. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Hiding in a safehouse, Orsen dreams himself fully into a Vessian life and wakes speaking only the dead language, unable to recall his own mother's face. Jude coaxes him back with stories of their brief weeks together. Emotional beat: identity slipping like sand.

chapters.title: Blood on the Inventory
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Thorn breaches the safehouse; Jude's mentor Pellam dies buying them time, whispering that he helped draft the original contract and has waited decades to atone. Emotional beat: guilt inherited alongside the child.

chapters.title: The Road Out of the Map
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Fleeing east, they cross terrain that grows increasingly Vessian — roads straightening into old processional ways, villages humming songs no one taught them. The erased country is bleeding back through. Emotional beat: awe and mounting urgency.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Captured by Guild wardens, Jude faces Corvane again, who reveals the Guild plans to bind Orsen permanently into the ledgers — a living asset, a country in a cage. Jude escapes using a door he was never authorized to know. Emotional beat: loyalty finally breaking.

chapters.title: The Thorn's Grief
chapters.summary: The Thorn's POV. It corners them at a river ford but falters when Orsen speaks its true name — it was once Vessia's royal executioner, made flesh from the country's shame. It lets them pass. Emotional beat: even vengeance longs to be remembered.

chapters.title: Doorways of the Drowned Country
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Guided by inherited memory, Orsen leads Jude across a drowned valley to the threshold of Vessia's stored heart — a door standing alone in open water. His memories now arrive faster than his own thoughts. Emotional beat: the heir becoming the country.

chapters.title: The Guild's Army
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Corvane arrives with wardens and ledger-magic to seize the door, offering Orsen immortality inside the Guild's pages. Jude publicly renounces his nineteen years of service and reads the contract's return clause aloud. Emotional beat: defiance as homecoming.

chapters.title: Orsen Speaks
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Before the assembled forces, the child formally asks for his country's return in the old tongue — then stops, feeling what restoration would mean: millions of stored souls poured back into a world that moved on. Emotional beat: the weight of inheritance fully understood.

chapters.title: The Choice of Doors
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The Thorn returns, not to kill but to testify, showing both sides what Vessia's preservation has cost — a people neither alive nor mourned. Orsen chooses a third path: open the door, let Vessia end, and carry its memory out as story instead of possession. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into wisdom.

chapters.title: Letting the Country Die
chapters.summary: Climax. Jude's POV. As Corvane tries to force the binding, Jude turns the key, the Thorn holds the wardens, and the door opens — light, names, and two centuries of held breath pouring free. Vessia ends not with a scream but with a sigh heard in every language. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Price of the Keeper
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The contract demands payment for breach: a keeper's name surrendered to the ledgers. Jude gives his willingly; Corvane, broken by the sight of freed souls, tears up the Guild's claim instead and walks into exile. Emotional beat: sacrifice met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: A Boy Called Orsen
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With Vessia gone, the inherited memories settle into quiet heritage rather than haunting. Orsen chooses to keep the name, adopted by the reformed Guild as its first honest archivist. Emotional beat: peace after possession.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Page
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shared POV. Years later, a nameless keeper tends the same gate while Orsen teaches children the old tongue as a living language, not a relic. On the last page of the great ledger, someone has written: 'Vessia was here, and was loved.' Emotional beat: memory as inheritance freely given.
